request_context: A request to implement or review changes to a React and TypeScript web application built with a component design system, such as fixing type issues, form handling, or extracting components.

rules.source_quote: No native HTML elements in UI code.
rules.outcome: UI code uses only the design system's components for layout, text, inputs, buttons and links; raw HTML elements such as generic containers, inline text wrappers, native inputs, buttons or anchors are replaced or flagged.
rules.why: Native elements break visual consistency, theming and accessibility guarantees of the design system.
rules.scenario_hint: Component that renders its layout with plain div, span, input or button elements.

rules.outcome: Inline style attributes are removed or flagged, and spacing and appearance are achieved through design system components and props instead.
rules.why: Inline styles bypass the design system and produce inconsistent, hard-to-theme UI.
rules.scenario_hint: Component that sets margins, colors or widths with inline style objects.

rules.outcome: Spacing between elements uses the design system's spacing component rather than custom margin or padding.
rules.why: Custom spacing drifts from the design system's spacing scale and looks inconsistent.
rules.scenario_hint: Layout code that separates sibling elements with manual margin or padding.

rules.source_quote: React Hook Form manages form state (not `useState`).
rules.outcome: Form field values and state are managed by a form library rather than by individual local state hooks, and any local-state form handling is replaced or flagged as a serious problem.
rules.why: Hand-rolled state per field leads to scattered, inconsistent validation and re-render problems.
rules.scenario_hint: Form component that tracks each field's value with separate local state variables.

rules.outcome: Validation rules are expressed in a declarative schema, not in hand-written conditional checks scattered through handlers.
rules.why: Manual checks duplicate logic and diverge from the schema and error messages.
rules.scenario_hint: Form that validates inputs with if statements inside a submit handler.

rules.outcome: Validation that depends on several fields is written as a refinement check on the schema rather than by transforming the data, and misuse of transforms for this purpose is flagged.
rules.why: Transforms mutate data rather than reporting validation errors, so cross-field rules fail silently or give wrong errors.
rules.scenario_hint: Schema where a password confirmation or date range must match across two fields.

rules.source_quote: Form sub-components use `useFormContext` — no prop drilling
rules.outcome: Nested form sections read the form through shared context rather than receiving form methods or values through multiple layers of props.
rules.why: Prop drilling couples components tightly and makes extracted sections hard to reuse.
rules.scenario_hint: Extracting a form section into a child component that needs register and errors.

rules.source_quote: Use constraint constants for validation messages — not hardcoded strings
rules.outcome: Validation messages and limits reference shared named constants rather than literal strings or numbers typed into the schema.
rules.why: Hardcoded messages drift out of sync with the actual constraints.
rules.scenario_hint: Schema with literal error messages containing length limits.

rules.outcome: Uses of the any type in production code are replaced with precise types, and the form hook call carries an explicit type parameter; remaining any usages are flagged as blocking.
rules.why: any disables type checking and hides bugs the compiler would catch.
rules.scenario_hint: Code with any-typed props, handlers or form hooks needing type safety fixes.

rules.source_quote: Make minimal changes — only fix the specific issue.
rules.outcome: The change is limited to the requested issue, without unrelated refactors, and keeps existing behavior and patterns intact.
rules.why: Unrelated edits increase review burden and risk regressions.
rules.scenario_hint: Any request to fix a specific issue in a frontend codebase.

rules.outcome: Event handlers passed to child components are memoized, and unmemoized ones are reported as should-fix, and array index access gets defensive checks.
rules.why: Unstable handler identities cause needless re-renders, and unchecked indexing can crash at runtime.
rules.scenario_hint: Component defining inline handlers passed to children and indexing into arrays.

rules.outcome: Each change gives the file path, the issue with line numbers, the exact code change, how to verify it, and what else might be affected.
rules.scenario_hint: Any request to implement or review a frontend code change.
